senses.gloss: ch. samethe washing of hands and feet.
units: <cite ref="Targum of II Chronicles 4:6">Targ. II Chr. IV, 6</cite>.—
<cite ref="Yoma 32a:1">Yoma 32ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ בתרא</he> the last ablution of the high priest (after putting off the priestly garments); a. e.
<cite ref="Pesachim 101a:6">Pes. 101ᵃ</cite> <he>בק׳ דהכא וכ׳</he> with the Ḳiddush that you hear here with me you will not have complied with the duty of &c.

<cite ref="Pesachim 106a:9">Ib. 106ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ רבה</he> the large Ḳiddush (jestingly for ‘small’), i.e. the mere blessing over wine preceding the meal on the festive day, contrad. to the Ḳiddush on the festive eve.
<cite ref="Megillah 27b:21">Meg. 27ᵇ</cite> <he>לא הוה לי ק׳ וכ׳</he> I had no wine for Ḳiddush, so I pawned &c.; a. fr.
<cite ref="Sotah 49a">Sot. 49ᵃ</cite> <he>ק׳ דסדרא</he> the Ḳ. recited after the lesson of the day (v. Rashi a. l.).
Y. B. Kam. IX, end, 7ᵃ מידמכא … אהן קי׳ דברתי when she was dying, she said, this is my daughter’s betrothal-gift (belongs to her); [prob. to be read: קַדִּישָׁא or קָדָשָׁא ring].
